extracted.intended_audience: contracting officers, procurement officials, and contractors drafting or applying warranty/deficiency clauses in federal supply, service, construction, or R&D contracts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory/example contract clauses governing when to use warranty clauses, what provisions they must contain (duration, notice, remedies, liability), factors to consider, and sample warranty/correction-of-deficiencies language for federal procurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of a warranty clause
rubrics_metrics.description: A warranty clause gives the Government a contractual right to assert claims regarding the deficiency of supplies or services furnished notwithstanding other contractual provisions pertaining to acceptance, and allows additional time after acceptance to assert rights to correction of defects, reperformance, equitable adjustment, or other remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value depends on circumstances; clause may be tailored to fit individual procurement or class of procurements (see § 1.324-3(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use warranty clause only when in Government's best interest
rubrics_metrics.description: A warranty clause shall be used when it is found to be in the best interest of the Government after analysis of the factors listed in § 1.324-3(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision requires weighing listed factors and may be made for individual procurements or classes of procurements (§ 1.324-2(a), § 1.324-3(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include warranty clause in cost-reimbursement contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: A warranty clause shall not be included in cost-reimbursement type contracts because warranty aspects of the Inspection of Supplies and Correction of Defects clause are sufficient to protect Government interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit prohibition for cost-reimbursement contracts (§ 1.324-2(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Warranty must not limit rights under Inspection clause
rubrics_metrics.description: Any warranty clause included in a contract shall not limit any rights afforded to the Government by the provisions of the Inspection clause relating to latent defects, fraud, and gross mistakes that amount to fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistency between warranty clause and other warranty provisions in the contract, especially when performance specifications are used (§ 1.324-2(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision authority for using warranty clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for certain commercial/military/guide-spec warranties, the Head of a Procuring Activity or designee shall decide whether to use a warranty clause, for individual procurements or classes of procurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-maker must consider the § 1.324-3(b) factors (§ 1.324-3(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor: nature of the item and its end use
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the nature of the item and how it will be used when deciding whether to include a warranty clause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as the first factor to consider in § 1.324-3(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor: cost of the warranty and effect of price competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the cost of the warranty and the degree of price competition as it may affect that cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance warranty cost against market competition effects (§ 1.324-3(b)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor: criticalness of achieving specified performance and design specs
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider how critical it is to achieve specified performance capabilities and design specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher criticalness favors including a warranty (§ 1.324-3(b)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor: cost of correction or replacement absent a warranty
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the cost to correct or replace defective items, either by the contractor or another source, if no warranty exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High corrective cost supports use of a warranty (§ 1.324-3(b)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor: administrative cost and difficulty of enforcing the warranty
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider how administratively costly or difficult it will be to enforce a warranty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If enforcement is impractical or costly, that weighs against warranty inclusion (§ 1.324-3(b)(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor: ability to take advantage of the warranty (storage/time/distance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether agencies can practically make use of the warranty given storage time, distance from source, or other factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ability to use warranty is limited, a warranty may be less useful (§ 1.324-3(b)(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor: warranty as deterrent against supplying defective goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the operation of the warranty as a deterrent against furnishing defective or nonconforming supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deterrent value is a benefit to weigh (§ 1.324-3(b)(7)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor: extent of Government reliance on contractor inspection/quality control
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the extent to which Government acceptance will be based upon contractor inspection or quality control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Greater reliance on contractor QC may increase need for a warranty (§ 1.324-3(b)(8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor: whether Government inspection system alone provides adequate protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether, because of the nature of the items, the Government inspection system would not be likely to provide adequate protection without a warranty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inspection alone is insufficient, include a warranty (§ 1.324-3(b)(9)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor: reliability of contractor's quality program
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the contractor’s present quality program is reliable enough to provide adequate protection without a warranty, or whether a warranty would induce an effective quality program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unreliable quality program favors a warranty; a strong program may make warranty unnecessary (§ 1.324-3(b)(10)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor: reliance on brand-name integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether reliance on a brand-name's integrity obviates the need for a warranty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brand reputation may reduce warranty need (§ 1.324-3(b)(11)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor: customary warranty practice for commercial components
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether a warranty is regularly given for a commercial component of a more complex end item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customary commercial practice supports including comparable warranties (§ 1.324-3(b)(12)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor: criticalness of item for personnel protection (safety)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider criticalness of the item for protection of personnel (e.g., safety in flight).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety-critical items favor warranties (§ 1.324-3(b)(13)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor: stage of development and state of the art
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the item's stage of development and the state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Less mature items may warrant different warranty treatment (§ 1.324-3(b)(14)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor: customary trade practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider customary trade practices in deciding whether to include a warranty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align with trade customs where appropriate (§ 1.324-3(b)(15)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking or notice requirement for warranted items
rubrics_metrics.description: When a warranty clause is used in a supply contract, consideration should be given to requiring that warranted items be marked or that notice of the warranty be otherwise furnished with the items to inform storage/stock/use personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required marking need not state the complete warranty; a short statement of existence, duration, and whom to notify is normally sufficient; contracting officer should weigh feasibility and cost (§ 1.324-3(c)(1)-(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility and cost-benefit of requiring marking/notice
rubrics_metrics.description: In deciding whether to require marking or notice, the contracting officer shall consider contractor feasibility of marking and the cost to the Government relative to probable benefit in enforcing the warranty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance practicality and enforcement benefit (§ 1.324-3(c)(2)(i)-(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting officer action upon notification of defect
rubrics_metrics.description: When notified of a defect in warranted items, the contracting officer should ascertain whether the warranty is currently in effect and ensure proper and timely notice of the defect is given to the contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely validation of warranty status is required (§ 1.324-3(c)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Guide Specifications' warranties in construction contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Warranties required by applicable Guide Specifications shall be included in advertised or negotiated construction contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory inclusion for Guide Specs (§ 1.324-3(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial warranties permitted when customary and not excessive
rubrics_metrics.description: In procurements involving commercial supplies/services or construction, the contracting officer may include a warranty clause standard or customary in the trade, or substantially similar to and not in excess of a standard/customary trade warranty, provided after review of § 1.324-3(b) factors it is in the Government's best interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows use of trade-standard warranties when appropriate (§ 1.324-4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clause must state duration of the warranty
rubrics_metrics.description: The terms and conditions of a warranty clause must state the duration of the warranty; it may cover defects existing at delivery or defects developing before expiration of a specified period or event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duration may be expressed as time after delivery, miles/hours of use, occurrence of event, etc. (§ 1.324-5(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clause must include notice period for reporting defects
rubrics_metrics.description: A warranty clause must include a specified period during which notice must be given to the contractor of any defects or nonconformance; notice period normally starts at delivery or acceptance but may start later when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conformance cannot be determined until use, notice period may begin when items are put to use or at last delivery (§ 1.324-5(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit contractor liability when Government specifies design precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Government specifies design, precise tolerances, materials, measurements, tests, or inspection requirements, contractor liability for defects/nonconformance should usually be limited to those existing at time of delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design-specified procurements typically limit post-delivery liability (§ 1.324-5(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend liability when performance specifications used
rubrics_metrics.description: Where performance specifications are used and design is of minor importance, contractor liability may extend to defects or nonconformance arising after delivery or acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate to consider extending warranty to post-delivery defects when performance specs govern (§ 1.324-5(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinary remedy: return for correction or replacement; special items may require broader remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily, remedy to return nonconforming supplies to contractor for correction or replacement should satisfy Government needs; but for supplies (e.g., subsistence or drugs) where correction/replacement is inadequate, clause should provide for Government return/disposal/replace and contractor liability for resulting costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contractor liability for costs occasioned to Government when correction/replacement insufficient (§ 1.324-5(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: In-place correction when return impractical
rubrics_metrics.description: When it is impractical to return an article for correction (e.g., installed equipment), clause should provide that Government may correct or require contractor to correct the article in place at contractor’s expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when removal/return would be substantially expensive or disruptive (§ 1.324-5(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Warrant particular aspects of an item when entire-item warranty not advisable
rubrics_metrics.description: If a warranty for the entire item is not advisable, require a warranty for particular aspects (installation, components, accessories, parts, subassemblies, preservation, packaging, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor warranty scope to protect specific vulnerable aspects (§ 1.324-5(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pricing warranty costs in fixed-price incentive contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: In fixed-price incentive contracts, estimated costs for the warranty should normally be considered in establishing the incentive target price; prior to establishing total final price, all warranty costs shall be considered in negotiating final total negotiated cost; after total final price is established, contractor compliance with warranty is at its expense with no increase in total final price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable adjustments under the warranty clause governed by Incentive Price Revision clause (§ 1.324-6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Warranty of Supplies clause: basic warranty language required
rubrics_metrics.description: Example clause requires contractor to warrant (i) all supplies free from defects in material or workmanship and conforming to specifications and other contract requirements; and (ii) preservation/packaging/packing/marking/shipment preparation/method conform to contract requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clause includes blanks for specific warranty period and notice period (see notes 1 and 2) (§ 1.324-7(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer options on breach of warranty (supplies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon written notice of breach, Contracting Officer may (i) require prompt correction or replacement, or (ii) retain supplies with equitable price reduction; if sampling inspection applies, CO may determine quantity subject to remedy per sampling procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides CO flexibility; sampling procedures can limit scope (§ 1.324-7(b)-(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling procedures and projection of warranty sampling results
rubrics_metrics.description: When inspection is by sampling, conformance for warranty action shall be determined per applicable sampling procedures; for sampling, CO may group supplies and project sampling results to other supplies in same shipment or other shipments provided remaining supplies reasonably representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original inspection lot size need not be reconstituted; substitutions of alternate paragraphs permitted for sampling contexts (§ 1.324-7(c) and following).

rubrics_metrics.name: CO options for grouped-supply warranty actions
rubrics_metrics.description: For grouped supplies subject to warranty action, the CO may (i) require equitable price adjustment, (ii) screen supplies at contractor’s expense and return nonconforming supplies for correction, (iii) require contractor to screen supplies at Government-designated depots and correct/replace nonconforming items, or (iv) return grouped supplies for contractor screening/correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies remedies and screening responsibilities for sampled/grouped lots (§ 1.324-7(c)(i)-(iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Government-borne transportation where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternate paragraph may provide that transportation incident to correction or replacement will be at Government's expense; appropriate when warranty cost otherwise prohibitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute paragraph (d) when desirable to have Government pay transportation for correction/replacement (§ 1.324-7(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor must proceed to correct even if dispute exists about responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If contractor does not agree he is responsible to correct/replace, he must nevertheless proceed per CO written request; if later determined not defective, an equitable adjustment will be made; failure to agree to equitable adjustment is a dispute under Disputes clause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures prompt correction actions despite disagreement; preserves dispute resolution (§ 1.324-7(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor transportation liability limits for return/correction
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Government returns supplies for correction or replacement, contractor liable for transportation charges and responsibility while in transit, but liability shall not exceed cost equal to usual commercial method of shipment between contract destination and contractor’s plant and return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caps contractor's transport liability to usual commercial cost (§ 1.324-7(d)/(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to correct before Government remedies (10-day default)
rubrics_metrics.description: If contractor fails or refuses to correct/replace nonconforming supplies within 10 days (or longer period authorized by CO) after receipt of notice, CO may correct or replace and charge contractor for Government-incurred cost; CO may dispose of nonconforming supplies for contractor’s account if timely disposition instructions not furnished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default period is illustrative; CO may authorize longer periods; disposal and reimbursement provisions apply (§ 1.324-7(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrected or replacement supplies subject to same warranty provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any supplies or parts corrected or furnished in replacement pursuant to the clause shall be subject to all the provisions of the clause to the same extent as supplies initially delivered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures remedies and obligations persist for corrected/replaced items (§ 1.324-7(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to agree on determinations under warranty is a disputes-clause issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to agree upon any determination to be made under the warranty clause shall be a dispute concerning a question of fact within the meaning of the Disputes clause of the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disagreements escalate to formal dispute resolution (§ 1.324-7(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'supplies' includes related services
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'supplies' as used in the warranty clause includes related services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies scope of term within the clause (§ 1.324-7(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service warranty clause: basic elements for services contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor warrants all services performed will be free from defects in workmanship and will conform to contract requirements at time of acceptance; CO gives written notice of defects and may require correction/reperformance at no cost or elect equitable adjustment if correction not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If contractor's design used, insert 'design and' before 'workmanship' (§ 1.324-8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of Deficiencies: definitions and general applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'deficiency' (condition not in compliance with contract requirements) and 'correction' (actions necessary to eliminate deficiencies); rights/remedies are in addition to and not affected by inspection/acceptance conclusive provisions and clause applies only to deficiencies discovered within a specified time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clause authorized for systems/equipment where performance specs or design are of major importance; blanks require insertion of specific time limits (§ 1.324-9(a)-(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for notice, contractor recommendations, and CO directions (Correction of Deficiencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: If CO determines a deficiency exists, he shall promptly notify contractor within specified time; contractor must promptly submit recommendations and supporting information; CO then, within a specified period after receiving recommendations, may direct correction, partial correction, or determine no correction required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides timeline-driven exchange and contractor obligation to propose corrective actions (§ 1.324-9(c)(1)-(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor obligation to correct deficiencies at no increase in contract price
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor shall promptly comply with any timely written direction to correct or partially correct a deficiency at no increase in contract price and furnish data/reports applicable to correction at no increase in contract price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractor bears correction cost unless parties agree to amend contract with equitable consideration (§ 1.324-9(c)(3)-(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: No extension of performance time or price due to correction obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Government is not responsible for extensions or delays in scheduled deliveries or periods of performance resulting from the contractor's obligations to correct deficiencies, nor for any adjustment of delivery schedule or performance period, except as agreed in a supplemental agreement with adequate consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clause shall not be construed as obligating Government to increase contract price (§ 1.324-9(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation charges and in-transit responsibility for corrections (Correction of Deficiencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: When Government returns supplies to contractor for correction or replacement, contractor liable for transportation charges up to cost equal to usual commercial method of shipment from designated destination to contractor's plant and return, and contractor bears responsibility while in transit; similarly for corrected/replacement shipment back to Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-part liability for both return-to-contractor and return-to-Government legs; details in § 1.324-9(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies if contractor fails to correct deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: If contractor fails to present recommendations, correct deficiencies, or furnish required data, CO shall give written notice setting period to cure; if not cured, CO may obtain recommendations, correct or replace supplies/services and charge contractor, dispose of nonconforming supplies for contractor's account, obtain applicable data/reports, and charge costs to contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates CO's remedial options and cost recovery mechanisms (§ 1.324-9(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrected replacements and reperformed services are subject to the same provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any supplies corrected or furnished in replacement and services reperformed pursuant to the Correction of Deficiencies clause are subject to all provisions of the clause to the same extent as initially accepted supplies/services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures continuing applicability to subsequent corrections (§ 1.324-9(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction warranty: one-year remedy period after final acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor shall remedy at his own expense any failure of the work to conform to contract specifications and any defect in material, workmanship, or design (excluding Government-furnished design) provided Government gives notice promptly after discovery but not later than one year after final acceptance (or one year from date Government takes possession of part of the work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractor must also remedy resultant damage and restore work; Government may replace/repair at contractor expense if contractor fails (§ 1.324-10(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontractor/manufacturer/supplier warranties enforced by contractor
rubrics_metrics.description: All subcontractors', manufacturers', and suppliers' warranties and guaranties respecting any part of the work are deemed obtained and shall be enforced by the contractor as agent and for the benefit of the Government without necessity of separate transfer or assignment; CO may direct contractor to require written execution to Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures Government benefit from downstream warranties without separate assignments (§ 1.324-10(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Repaired or replaced construction work also subject to warranty
rubrics_metrics.description: Any work repaired or replaced pursuant to the construction warranty clause shall be subject to the provisions of the clause to the same extent as work originally performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rights and remedies are in addition to other contract rights (§ 1.324-10(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference: commercial warranty clauses allowed in ordering/request forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial warranty clause may be used in accordance with § 1.324-4 of this chapter in standard forms (e.g., SF 1155, SF 30) and procurement procedures where commercial warranty permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures consistency across procurement forms and procedures (PART 3 / § 3.608-2 notes).
